title: ElmHaven retail pilot — raw call digest
content:
Context: ElmHaven is a mid-market retail chain (120 stores). Pilot goal: in-store assistant for returns and inventory lookup, must run with customer VPC + private-control-plane. They care most about latency at peak (checkout window) and PII handling.

Call summary (2026-02-18, 30m):
- Attendees: Priya (CS), Miguel (SRE), Samira (Solutions Eng), Evan (ElmHaven IT), Lauren (ElmHaven Ops), Raj (ElmHaven Security)
- Quick ask: deploy a private plane instance behind ElmHaven VPC, single-model chat endpoint for returns/responses. 95th perc latency target: <=120ms token generation on average for 64-token responses at peak.
- Traffic estimate: normal day 60 qps across region; peak (holiday/test) bursts to ~300 qps for short windows. Typical prompt size: 120–220 tokens input, want streaming response.
- Data policy: no customer PII should leave ElmHaven network. They want optional on-prem model (air-gapped) if pilot shows value; first phase: private-control-plane with model in our dedicated subnet (customer-managed).

Technical constraints & gotchas noted: (raw, scribbles)
- VPC peering: ElmHaven insists on AWS side-proxy NAT + strict IP allowlist. Need clear list of egress IPs and TLS SNI behavior.
- Firewall rules block nonstandard ports; ops will only open 443/22. We need to confirm websocket streaming over TLS works with their TLS inspection devices (some of their stores have TLS MITM boxes for scanning).
- Tokenization mismatch: their current NLU uses SentencePiece models for internal product IDs; we should verify model tokenizer vs their ID scheme to avoid truncation of SKUs in outputs.
- Embedding usage: they want similarity search for receipts in phase 2. Keep an eye on index size (their receipts avg 2KB). Potentially need to shard embeddings and consider 8-bit quantized models for cost.
- Peak GPU type: customer prefers cost-efficient A10G/RTX-class. For latency target we may need A100/Trident for initial canary; call it out as tradeoff.
- KV-cache warmup: their flows include repeated prompts with store context; recommend prefix caching to reduce cold-token cost. Note: cache invalidation policy must be explicit for returns window (per-store contexts).
- Logging/audit: they require event-level audit logs retained 12 months. That is above default—storage + retention pricing impact.

Open questions (we must resolve before next step):
1) ElmHaven legal wants exact wording for where tokens are stored and whether we retain prompt text after processing. Need a short paragraph for legal to sign. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-02-25.
2) Are we allowed to run streaming websocket through their TLS inspection devices? If not, fallback will be chunked HTTP polling which increases latency. Owner: Miguel to validate with Evan. Due: 2026-02-22.
3) Do they want model outputs to be post-processed to redact potential SSNs? They asked for PII-safe defaults. Samira to propose redaction rules and eval prompts. Due: 2026-02-28.
4) Our default quantization profile may alter subtle instruction following; ElmHaven wants QA with their prompt suite (~120 seed prompts). Need dataset from Lauren. Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-03-05.

Action items (concrete):
- Miguel: produce a minimal IP allowlist and network diagram for ElmHaven NAT/proxy interactions and websocket behavior (deliverable: diagram + port checklist). Due 2026-02-22.
- Priya: write a one-paragraph data residency/retention statement for legal. Attach to pilot SOW. Due 2026-02-25.
- Samira: create an eval harness (5–10 step smoke tests) for their prompt set and initial quality targets; include redaction checks. Push to infra repo PR. Due 2026-03-05.
- Evan (customer): provide sample receipts (anonymized) and SKU examples, list of store IP ranges (or /16s) we should expect. Due 2026-02-26.
- Solutions: propose a fallback plan for stores with TLS inspection (limit: chunked polling). Document latency delta and UX impact. Owner: Samira + Miguel. Due 2026-02-28.

Quick rough sizing note (back-of-envelope):
- If we need to consistently handle 300 qps peak and maintain <120ms 95th, plan for 4 dedicated A10G-like instances with optimized batching and low-latency kernel, or 2 A100-style nodes with higher throughput. Cost delta estimate: dedicated reserved monthly vs. private on-prem one-off. Need infra to produce exact numbers.

Risks flagged:
- TLS inspection could break streaming and degrade SLOs.
- Audit retention request will increase storage + egress costs and may slow down initial sign-off.
- Tokenization/ID issues could produce hallucinated SKUs; critical to validate with sample SKUs.

Notes-to-self / things to remember:
- Avoid using term 'onprem' in customer-facing docs; use 'private deployment / on-site model' per Raj's preference.
- Use nontechnical summary for Lauren, technical appendix for Evan.
- Capture a short demo script focusing on returns resolution <2 mins end-to-end (happy path + fallback path).

Next meeting: 2026-02-24 11:00 PT. Proposed agenda: network confirmation, legal paragraph sign-off, demo runbook, decide canary GPU type.

Quick links here (put in Jira ticket CH-4321):
- Draft SOW template link for pilots
- Sample prompt set placeholder: "elmhaven_prompts_v1.txt" (we need actual upload)

End raw digest.

(Formatting intentionally loose — this is a working capture, will extract for tidy playbook after next sync.)
